subject: Reserved commit term negotiation — 36mo anchoring, soft-start slots, and throughput SLA
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Casey Taylor <ctaylor@neptune-analytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Reserved commit term negotiation — 12/24/36mo options, soft-start slots, and throughput SLAs

Hi Casey —

Thanks again for the time last week. Per our discussion I pulled together three term structures we typically offer for Dedicated (attached: neptune_proposal_v3.pdf):

- 12 month: higher unit price, minimal commit ramp (best for short pilots)
- 24 month: mid price with 60% of committed throughput guaranteed after month 3
- 36 month: deepest discount, stronger throughput guarantees, and dedicated pool anchoring

A few implementation details I want to highlight:
- Start date: we can target an \"activation window\" (start gate) rather than a single calendar day — this helps with infra scheduling.
- Soft-start slots: first 30–45 days we reserve burst capacity for onboarding (no extra charge for reasonable onboarding spikes).
- Ramp schedule: typical obligates ~30% utilization first 3 months, 60% by month 6, full steady-state by month 12 for 36mo deals; we can customize.
- SLA/credits: we provide throughput guarantees and monthly uptime SLOs; credit structure is negotiable by tier.

Can you confirm: 1) preferred term (12/24/36), 2) target start month (June/July/Aug), and 3) whether you want us to include a clause for +/- start-date flexibility? Once we have those I’ll get Ben to map the pricing and Monica to confirm SLA tolerances.

Thanks —
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0199

Attachment: neptune_proposal_v3.pdf
From: Casey Taylor <ctaylor@neptune-analytics.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@neptune-analytics.com
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved commit term negotiation — 12/24/36mo options, soft-start slots, and throughput SLAs

Soojin —

Appreciate the options. High-level answers:
1) We are leaning strongly to 36 months for budget predictability, assuming the unit economics and credits line up.
2) Target start: were aiming for a July 2027 activation, but procurement will want a +/- window to accommodate internal approvals.
3) Start-date flexibility: procurement asks for at least +/- 30 days.

A few open questions from procurement (Im copying them):
- How do you define guaranteed throughput vs. best-effort? We need concrete measurement (tokens/min or requests/sec) and measurement windows.
- For onboarding spikes, can soft-start bursts be materially larger than steady-state? We anticipate a data ingest workload for two weeks that might exceed ramp percentages.
- Any constraints for reserved commit conversion if we underutilize in year 1 — can credits roll forward or be converted to additional caching/embedding units?

If you can provide a more explicit SLA/credit table and a sample ramp schedule tied to numeric throughput values, we can accelerate approvals.

Best,
Casey Taylor
Head of Platform Strategy, Neptune Analytics
ctaylor@neptune-analytics.com
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Casey Taylor <ctaylor@neptune-analytics.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Mar 2027 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved commit term negotiation — 12/24/36mo options, soft-start slots, and throughput SLAs

Casey —

Thanks for the clarity. I attached a worked pricing model (throughput_modeling.xlsx) and sketched an SLA/credit table below for the 36-month anchor:

Pricing (36mo anchor):
- Base reserved commit: 18 vGPU-pool units (NVIDIA H100 equivalent) — committed monthly throughput = 1.2M tokens/min sustained
- Effective discounted unit price: 42% off public hosted rate (applies to committed tokens); overages billed at 60% of on-demand rate.

Proposed ramp schedule (numeric):
- Month 0 (activation window): provisioning complete; onboarding soft-start slots available up to 2x baseline for first 14 days
- Months 1-3: target 30% of committed throughput (~360k tokens/min avg)
- Months 4-6: target 60% (~720k tokens/min avg)
- Months 7-12: linear ramp to 100% (~1.2M tokens/min avg)

SLA & credit table (monthly measurement):
- Uptime SLO: 99.5% monthly availability for the Dedicated pool (exclusions: scheduled maintenance, force majeure)
- Throughput SLO: monthly delivered sustained throughput within 10% of committed tokens/min = no credit; 10-25% shortfall = 5% monthly credit; 25-50% shortfall = 15% credit; >50% = 30% credit (credits applied to next invoice)

Flexibility: we can allow a +/- 30 day start gate. If Neptune needs an extended window (45 days) we can include a one-time adjustment to ramp milestones.

Next steps: Soojin, can you confirm whether the 18 vGPU-pool sizing aligns with Neptunes expected concurrency? If yes, well push a term sheet and Monica will validate the credit language operationally.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Director, Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Attachment: throughput_modeling.xlsx
From: Casey Taylor <ctaylor@neptune-analytics.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 14:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved commit term negotiation — 12/24/36mo options, soft-start slots, and throughput SLAs

Ben / Soojin —

Thanks, thats much more concrete and helpful. High-level responses from procurement & engineering:
- 18 vGPU pool at 1.2M tokens/min is OK as a starting anchor but engineering will want a 30% buffer on peak concurrency. Can we provision an option to add a 4-vGPU burst slice for the first 90 days?
- The throughput credit tiers look reasonable but procurement wants the measurement window specified (we suggest 7-day rolling windows for throughput shortfall detection rather than a single monthly snapshot).
- Start-date flexibility: procurement still prefers +/- 30 days hard, with an optional one-time extension to 60 days if Neptune hits a regulatory hold.

Im attaching procurements standard SOW redlines in-line here (forwarded). Please confirm whether the 7-day rolling window is acceptable and if the burst slice for onboarding can be formalized as an option in the term sheet.

Best,
Casey

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Casey Taylor <ctaylor@neptune-analytics.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: Finalizing term language — SLA tolerance, burst slice, and start gate flexibility

Hi Casey / team —

Following Bens draft and your procurement comments, heres Redwoods operational position for inclusion in the term sheet (we will mirror this in the attached redwood_final_term_sheet_neptune_v1.pdf):

1) Burst slice: we can include a one-time optional 4-vGPU burst slice for onboarding (available for the first 90 days). Usage during the burst is billed at the committed rate and does not trigger overage for the onboarding window.

2) Throughput measurement: we accept 7-day rolling window measurements for throughput SLO evaluation. Credits will be calculated on the first full week where shortfall thresholds are exceeded, aggregated monthly.

3) Start gate flexibility: standard +/- 30 day start gate. One-time extension to 60 days available with written notice and mutually agreed ramp adjustment.

4) SLA / credits: propose uptime SLO of 99.5% monthly. Throughput credit tiers to align with Bens table; credits applied as invoice adjustments or service credits per Neptune preference.

5) Underutilization: unused committed tokens in year 1 may be converted to a combination of credit rollover (up to 20% of unused) or one-time exchange to additional embedding/storage units (details in the term sheet).

If this matches Neptunes needs, well prepare the final DocuSign-ready term sheet and routing for signature (link included). We aim to have a countersigned agreement by mid-April to hit a July activation window.

Monica Patel
Director, Customer Success — Dedicated Deployments, Redwood Inference
